# task-7189c874: copy the marked panel into every equal panel

## Validated rule

Identify complete, uniform divider rows and/or columns that partition the grid into equally sized panels. Find the panel that contains the pattern/foreground marks against an otherwise uniform background; that is the source panel, and it need not be the bottom-right panel. Copy the source panel's entire contents by direct positional alignment into every panel, including the source's blank/background cells. Preserve all divider cells and output the original dimensions. Do not reflect or rotate the source.

Confirmed by one demo and one accepted test in this task:

- Demo (15x11): a full divider column (color 1) and divider row (color 1) partition the grid into four equal 7x5 panels. The top-right panel contains a sparse pattern on background 8; the other panels are blank. The output repeats the top-right panel's entire pattern into all four panels, preserving dividers. This directly shows that the source is the marked panel, not necessarily bottom-right.
- Accepted test (23x5): divider column 2 (color 2) and divider rows 7 and 15 (color 2) make six 7x2 panels. The middle-right panel (rows 8–14, cols 3–4, 0-indexed) contains marks on background 1. The accepted output copies this whole 7x2 panel into all six panels by local coordinates; divider lines remain unchanged. Thus the source can be in the middle band, and the pattern replicates both across rows and across columns.

## Additional accepted instance: 3x3 panel tiling

A 17x11 test had full divider rows 5 and 11 and full divider columns 3 and 7 (0-indexed), all color 4. These partitioned the non-divider cells into nine equal 5x3 panels. The uniquely marked source was the middle-left panel (rows 6–10, cols 0–2), with background color 1 and marks: color 7 at local coordinates (0,2) and (2,1), and color 9 at (1,0). Copy the full 5x3 source panel by local coordinates into all nine panels, including background cells, while preserving every divider. This confirms the rule extends to a 3x3 arrangement and a source panel in the middle row / leftmost column.

## Additional accepted instance: 2x2 panels, source bottom-left

A 9x19 test had a full divider row 4 and full divider column 9 (0-indexed), both color 8. These partitioned the grid into four equal 4x9 panels over background color 4. The uniquely marked source was bottom-left (rows 5–8, cols 0–8). Copy its complete panel positionally into the other three panels, including the background cells and all multicolor marks, while preserving the divider cross. The source pattern was:

```text
4 7 0 4 4 6 4 4 4
4 4 4 4 0 0 4 4 4
4 9 4 6 1 4 6 4 4
1 4 4 1 4 4 5 4 4
```

Accepted output confirms the entire source panel is copied to each equal panel, not just foreground cells. This adds a 2x2 arrangement with the source bottom-left.

## Additional accepted instance: 2x3 panels, source top-right

A 9x8 test had full divider row 4 and full divider columns 2 and 5 (0-indexed), all color 2. This formed six equal 4x2 panels (two panel rows by three panel columns), with background color 6. The uniquely marked source was the top-right panel (rows 0–3, columns 6–7): color 4 at local coordinate (2,0) and color 3 at (3,0). Copy the full panel by local coordinates into all six panels, including its background cells, preserving the divider lines. The accepted output confirms replication across a 2x3 arrangement with a source in the top-right.

## Application checks

1. Verify the full uniform divider lines and equal panel dimensions.
2. Locate the uniquely marked/non-background panel; do not assume it is bottom-right. If more than one distinct marked panel makes the source ambiguous, request a demo.
3. Copy every source-panel cell to the same local coordinate in every panel, including background values, and preserve divider cells.
4. Verify dimensions and row lengths. Avoid merely repeating marks in the source column/band: copy the whole panel across the entire partition.

## Additional accepted instance

A 13x13 test had uniform divider row 6 and divider column 6, both color 4, producing four 6x6 panels. The top-right panel was the uniquely marked panel, on background 2. Its complete 6x6 contents (including background cells) were copied positionally into all four panels, preserving the divider cross and the original 13x13 dimensions. This is another confirmed case where the source panel is top-right and the copy spans both dimensions.

## Additional accepted instance: 3x2 panels, source bottom-left

A 20x19 test had full divider rows 6 and 13 and a full divider column 9 (0-indexed), all color 9. The non-divider area formed six equal 6x9 panels (three panel rows by two panel columns). The uniquely marked source was the bottom-left panel (rows 14–19, columns 0–8), with background color 3 and marks in colors 0 and 6.
